title: Restructuring in the Local News Media
what_it_is: Restructuring in the Local News Media

sections.label: Government support for SPH proposal
sections.summary: The Ministry voiced Government support for SPH's proposal and committed to support the media business as it adapts for a digital future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: My Ministry has voiced the Government's support for SPH's proposal and committed to support the media business as it builds capabilities and adapts for a digital future.

sections.label: Trust in Singapore local media
sections.summary: Surveys reported Singaporeans' trust in local media at seven in 10 in 2020 and 62% in 2021, above global, US, UK and France figures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In a 2020 survey by the British pollster YouGov, seven in 10 Singaporeans said they trusted the local media's reporting on COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 2021, the Edelman trust barometer reported Singaporeans' trust in local media at 62% – above the global average of 51% and above the US, which is 45%; and UK and France, which were both at 37%.

sections.label: Formation of SPH
sections.summary: SPH was formed in 1984 through a merger of the English, Chinese and Malay language papers, with the Tamil press added in 1995.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 1984, SPH was formed through a merger of the English, Chinese and Malay language papers, with the Tamil press brought under its umbrella later in 1995.

sections.label: Global print advertising revenue decline
sections.summary: Global print advertising revenue is decreasing by 7% year on year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Global print advertising revenue is decreasing by 7% year on year.

sections.label: Disappearance of American and UK newspapers
sections.summary: Over a quarter of American newspapers disappeared in 15 years, halving newsroom jobs, and over half the UK lacks local newspapers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: More than a quarter of American newspapers have disappeared in the last 15 years, reducing the number of newsroom jobs by half.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In the UK, more than half the country is no longer served by their own local newspapers.

sections.label: News Corp 2020 loss
sections.summary: News Corp, one of the largest media groups, recorded a US$1.5 billion loss in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: News Corp, one of the largest media groups in the world, recorded a US$1.5 billion loss in 2020.

sections.label: Paper operating revenue fell
sections.summary: In the six years before the sale, the paper's operating revenue fell by 44%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In the six years before the sale, the paper's operating revenue fell by 44%.

sections.label: New York Times digital subscribers
sections.summary: The New York Times reached 7.5 million subscribers in 2020 but saw ad revenue plunge by 26% that year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The New York Times has done especially well in making the digital pivot, recently reaching 7.5 million subscribers in 2020, though it too saw ad revenue plunge by 26% the same year.

sections.label: SPH Media Jobs Support Scheme
sections.summary: Last year over $30 million was provided to SPH Media through the Jobs Support Scheme, with more prepared if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Last year, we also provided SPH Media with over $30 million through the national Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) and we were prepared to do more if the need arose.

sections.label: SPH circulation and digital investment
sections.summary: SPH's papers' circulation grew 5% from 2017 to 2020, with The Straits Times up about 20% and $50 million yearly digital investment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: SPH's papers' circulation has grown by 5% from 2017 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In fact, within this period, The Straits Times' print and digital circulation has grown by about 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: SPH has also made significant investments of about $50 million a year for the last five years to build digital capabilities and grow its readership.

sections.label: SPH media business loss
sections.summary: SPH announced its media business lost half its operating revenue in five years and posted a $11.4 million loss in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: SPH announced last week that its media business had lost half its operating revenue in the past five years and posted its first ever loss of $11.4 million in 2020.

sections.label: SPH media business restructuring transfer
sections.summary: SPH proposes transferring its media business to a Company Limited by Guarantee, capitalising a new subsidiary with $80 million cash and $30 million in shares and REITs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: SPH proposes to restructure and transfer the ownership of its media business to a Company Limited by Guarantee (CLG).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: It will first form a new subsidiary, transfer the media-related businesses and properties to the subsidiary and capitalise the subsidiary with $80 million of cash and $30 million worth of SPH shares and REITs.

sections.label: Government support for SPH restructuring
sections.summary: The Government supports SPH's restructuring proposal and is willing to provide funding support to the CLG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government therefore supports SPH's restructuring proposal and is willing to provide funding support to the CLG.

sections.label: Funding CLG digital innovation
sections.summary: The Government is willing to help fund the CLG in areas like digital innovation and capability development, with fiscal discipline and accountability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Government is willing to help fund the proposed CLG – while ensuring fiscal discipline and accountability – in areas like digital innovation and capability development, as part of a long-term sustainable business plan.

sections.label: Khaw Boon Wan CLG Chairman
sections.summary: Management shareholders agreed Mr Khaw Boon Wan should be CLG Chairman, and the Government stands ready to provide funding for digital innovation and capability development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: I also discussed this with the management shareholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: They have all agreed that, given the national importance of this undertaking and the scale of the challenge, the Chairman should be Mr Khaw Boon Wan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: With his high standing and more than 25 years of public service experience in various senior appointments, Mr Khaw will be able to provide strong strategic leadership for the CLG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: I am pleased to inform Members that Mr Khaw has agreed to be the Chairman of the CLG, and he will be sharing his thoughts on its way forward in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To ensure the long-term viability of the enterprise, the Government also stands ready to provide the CLG with funding in areas like digital innovation and capability development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The new media company must have a long-term, sustainable business model with different revenue sources, including traditional advertising and subscription revenues, complemented by Government funding and contributions from its management shareholders and benefactors as other components.

sections.label: Lifting SPH shareholding controls
sections.summary: After restructuring and transfer of the media business to the CLG, MCI will lift shareholding controls on the listed SPH entity, and the NPPA will apply to the new media company.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Subject to shareholder approval, after the restructuring is completed and the media business is transferred to the CLG, MCI will lift the shareholding controls imposed on the listed SPH entity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The NPPA will then apply to the new media company, under the CLG’s charge.

sections.label: Questions on grants and independence
sections.summary: Questions were asked about when the Government informed SPH of grants, capping grants, SPH's contribution, structures for editorial independence, and a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, when did the Government first inform SPH that it was prepared to extend grants to support its media business?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Government aim to cap the grants it extends, with the expectation that CLG will also secure other sources of funding from the private sector, for example?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The third question is with respect to some public documents that were released by SPH last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was decided that the SPH contribution towards the CLG would be, I quote, "arrived at after considering various factors, including the potential funding requirements of the media business for a few years".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My final two questions: what structures will the Government insist on to ensure the independence of the SPH CLG from possible Government's interference and to foster a culture of editorial independence across its titles?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And, finally, in view of the significant change in the sector, would the Government consider the formation of a Select Committee to allow members of the public and Singaporeans in particular to: (a) express what editorial standards they expect from the CLG, taxpayer-funded mainstream media; and (b) to express their views on how best the SPH CLG can ensure editorial independence from any government of the day?

sections.label: SPH received JSS
sections.summary: SPH received the JSS last year as part of the national scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In the case of SPH, specifically, as I mentioned, last year, they received the JSS, which was part of the national scheme.

sections.label: CLG funding and SPH contribution
sections.summary: Government funding is expected to be part of the CLG's funding mix, alongside advertising, circulation and subscription revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We fully expect the entity to seek out advertising revenue, circulation or subscription revenue and other sources of funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But we fully expect that Government funding will be a component of that funding matrix for the CLG.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: He asked if the SPH contribution which has been spelt out – which includes the transfer of two property assets which are related to the media business and also some other operating businesses which are linked to the media, in addition to the $80 million of cash and $30 million of SPH shares and REITs – he asked whether this is reasonable and why.

sections.label: Medium to long-term outlook
sections.summary: The medium- to long-term outlook remains challenging, though specifics of near-term numbers were not given.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Whilst I am unable to say specifics about what the numbers look like in the near term – SPH has said some about how they think it will continue to widen in terms of its deficit – I can say that the medium- to long-term outlook remains challenging.

sections.label: Surveys on trust in local media
sections.summary: Local IPS surveys validate that about 70% of Singaporeans trust local media.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I cited the YouGov survey and also the Edelman Trust Report.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I would add that even our local surveys, for example, by the IPS, validate this, saying that about 70% of Singaporeans, or seven out of 10, trust our local media.

sections.label: Funding CLG with financial discipline
sections.summary: The funding of the CLG is to be done with financial discipline and accountability in digital innovation and capability development.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Clearly, and as I said in my Ministerial Statement, we want to do this – and by this, I mean the funding of the CLG – with financial discipline and accountability in areas like digital innovation and capability development.

sections.label: Capability development for sustaining attention
sections.summary: Capability development is a means to sustaining or growing Singaporeans' attention, readership and following.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But it goes beyond that because the development of capabilities in the end is a means to a more important end.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And that end is sustaining, if not growing, the attention, the readership and the following from Singaporeans.

sections.label: Citizen attention as ultimate measure
sections.summary: Without people's attention the effort rings hollow, so the ultimate measure is how citizens respond to the news organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Because at the end of the day, if you do not have the eyeballs, the attention of people, then, the effort, in a sense, will ring hollow.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And our objective, when we talk about a trusted, professional, high quality news organisation, the ultimate measure of it, as I said in my response to the Leader of the Opposition, is in how our citizens respond to it and how much attention they give it – whether it is in terms of readership, dwell time; and this is especially so in the moment of crisis, which is when the truth and reliability of information becomes even more critical.

sections.label: Time for business transition
sections.summary: The business must be given enough time to transition to a more sustainable business model, with support rendered to the CLG without changing the relationship between news organisations and the Government and MCI.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The business must be given enough time to be able to transition to a more sustainable business model.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And that is something that we are now committed to do by rendering support to the CLG but without changing the nature of the relationship that we have today between these news organisations and the Government and MCI.

sections.label: CLG model and Government support
sections.summary: Moving from a listed company structure to a CLG model will let the company dedicate resources to digital pivoting, with Government support important.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I pointed out, I think the current structure, whilst there has been a considerable effort on the part of SPH to pivot to digital and they have made the investments I have mentioned, about $50 million a year over five years, but really, they need to do more and they need to do it in a more purposeful and quick way.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think that is something that if you talk to the editors and the journalists, they would say and that is also the experience that we see around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Therefore, I think, first, the fact that you are now moving out of a listed company structure into a CLG model will give that company the opportunity to dedicate the resources it needs for this purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And that is where I think the support from Government will also be important.

sections.label: Talent, strategic moves, other options
sections.summary: The CLG and management must bring in talent and make decisive strategic moves, and the proposal came from SPH management and Board assessing their business.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But going forward, the CLG and the management will have to bring in talent – in addition to what they already have within – to address this in a very direct way and start making the decisive strategic moves in that regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think the ability to make such moves and then back them with the resources and then find the talent to back it up, these are all going to be important differentiating factors in the change that has been proposed under the restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The second clarification is, has the Government consider other options such as privatising SPH so that the media unit is not subject to the market returns pressure, very much like SMRT, or even like the Mediacorp approach where the Government support the company with annual public service broadcasting grants?

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: First, we have to be very clear how the proposal came about.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is the result of SPH management and Board assessing their business, in particular, the media business and its prospects going forward; and then, putting forward a proposal which, in their assessment, achieves best the objective of ensuring the viability and success of the media business going forward, freed from the constraints of a listed company and its reporting structures and so on.

sections.label: SPH to explain to shareholders
sections.summary: SPH, its management, directors and advisers must explain the proposal to shareholders, while support is given to secure long-term sustainability of trusted news media.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is for SPH and its management and its directors and independent financial advisers and independent directors to explain to their shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We support it from the perspective of what needs to be done to secure the long-term sustainability of a quality, trusted news media in Singapore.

sections.label: Funding listed company dividends question
sections.summary: If funding goes to a listed company that makes profits and distributes dividends, the question arises whether taxpayers are subsidising returns to shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The problem is, if we channel a certain amount of funding to the listed company and the listed company then makes profits and then it distributes dividends to its shareholders, the question that can be asked is: is this a case of taxpayers subsidising returns to shareholders?

sections.label: Khaw Boon Wan CLG Chairman choice
sections.summary: The Government and management shareholders agreed on Mr Khaw Boon Wan as CLG Chairman, and it is asked whether the Government suggested him.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, he has acknowledged that due to the proposed change in the funding, there are some concerns about the implications of Government funding on the editorial direction of the newspaper.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And in the same breath, he just announced to us today that the Government and the management shareholders of SPH have agreed on the choice of the Chairman of the CLG to be Mr Khaw Boon Wan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, let me clarify that I am not questioning the personal integrity of Mr Khaw but the fact is that he is the former chairman of the People's Action Party and former Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask Minister: first of all, the choice of Mr Khaw, although he said it was by agreement between the Government and the management shareholders, am I to assume that it was the Government's suggestion that Mr Khaw takes on this role and the management shareholders agreed to that suggestion?

sections.label: Khaw Boon Wan chairing CLG
sections.summary: The question is whether Khaw Boon Wan being asked by management shareholders to chair the CLG creates editorial independence problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Second, I think the nub of her question really is that, with Mr Khaw Boon Wan being asked by the management shareholders to chair the CLG, whether this creates problems from the point of view of editorial independence.

sections.label: Media credibility and leadership appointments
sections.summary: What matters is not a perceived political hue in appointments but the character and capability of those involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Yet, we are where we are today – and I do not wish to canvass arguments all over again – but we are where we are today in terms of the credibility of our media, the trust that Singaporeans have in our media, through this array of leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think we should therefore be very clear that what matters is not a perceived political hue in the appointments, but rather in the substance of the character and capability of the people who are involved.

sections.label: Khaw Boon Wan choice for undertaking
sections.summary: The undertaking is major and of national importance, and the choice of Khaw Boon Wan was keenly wanted by management shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Make no mistake about it – this is a major undertaking and it is one that is of national importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think the choice of Mr Khaw Boon Wan is something that not just the Government but in fact the management shareholders were very keen on.

sections.label: What can you sell
sections.summary: This means answering what can be sold that is insightful, relevant and distinctive, to whom and at what price.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Which means, essentially, answering the question: what can you sell that is insightful, relevant and distinctive and provides an engaging audience experience, to whom and at what price?

sections.label: Funding and vernacular newspaper retention
sections.summary: The question asks whether other funding sources would include a mechanism to ensure vernacular newspapers are explicitly retained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Or if funding is given by other sources, will there be a mechanism to ensure that these vernacular newspapers, so important to our nation building, are explicitly retained?

sections.label: Preserving vernacular media voice
sections.summary: Industry stresses mean newsroom capacity would diminish, and vernacular media with smaller circulation are most at risk, so their voice should be preserved.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I said, the stresses that the industry is under today, in particular, SPH Media, means that if nothing were done, then the capacity within the newsrooms would diminish because cost cutting would be inevitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think amongst the first and most at-risk will be the vernacular media because they have got a smaller circulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If you take a purely business logic to this, then I think the outcomes can be quite detrimental from a national cohesion point of view.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, certainly, as I have said, we want to preserve the voice of our vernacular media.

sections.label: KPIs for CLG independence
sections.summary: Asks whether KPIs should be set and regularly measured to ensure public belief in the new CLG's independence and editorial independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, would the Minister consider – either the CLG doing this or the Government doing this – to set KPIs that are regularly measured to ensure that the public actually believes in the independence of the new CLG, in its editorial independence, and to measure that regularly, given that taxpayer monies will be pumped in?

sections.label: Editorial appointments and downsizing
sections.summary: States the Government does not veto senior editorial appointments, which are subject to management and shareholders, and asks about further downsizing and support for employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Government does not exercise a veto on those appointments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The decisions on those are made by management; shareholders have a say in that matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Government has a say on some other matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But when it comes to the senior editorial appointments, it is all subject to the management, shareholders' approval.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, is there likely to be any further downsizing as part of the transfer of SPH's media business to the CLG and, if so, will the Government ensure that any employees in transition are supported?

sections.label: Entire team moving over
sections.summary: States the proposal's terms are for the entire team to move over, so no attritions are intended.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The terms of the proposal, as I understand it as of now, are to have the entire team move over and, therefore, no attritions are intended.

sections.label: Commitment to vernacular media
sections.summary: States that vernacular media is treasured and nurtured, and that the commitment to it should remain during the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, I think it is something that is treasured, something that we have nurtured through the years and it is not something that we want to lose.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, certainly, in the course of this transition, we would want to ensure that that commitment to our vernacular media remains.

sections.label: Ballpark figure for CLG grant
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister can share any ballpark figure for the amount of taxpayer dollars going to the CLG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I would be surprised if the Government had not considered what would be the extent of the grant that it would extend to the CLG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, can the Minister share with us if there is any ballpark figure as to what is the amount of taxpayer dollars that will be going to the CLG?

sections.label: Select Committee on taxpayer-funded CLG
sections.summary: Notes differing views on journalism quality and standards, and cites that as the reason for the earlier question about a Select Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On the other hand, the English papers, "a major Cabinet reshuffle but now is not the time to read the tea leaves".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, there can be different views on the quality and the standards of journalism and it is for that reason that I put my earlier question to the Minister about a Select Committee and to try and get some understanding from the public what they expect of a taxpayer-funded CLG.

sections.label: Funding CLG and budget
sections.summary: The speaker says they went further than supporting restructuring by being prepared to fund the CLG, and funding will return to the Chamber as part of MCI's budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Not just to say that we support the restructuring – because we could have stopped there – but we went a step further to say that we would be prepared to fund the CLG.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is a significant point which should not be overlooked.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And, clearly, when the funding is finally decided upon, it will have to come back to this Chamber because it will be part of the budget of MCI and the Member and his party would have ample opportunity to ask all the specific questions.

sections.label: Preserving vernacular newspapers
sections.summary: The Minister said they would ask vernacular newspapers to be preserved after restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Just now, Minister said that they would ask vernacular newspapers to be preserved after restructuring.

sections.label: Commitment to vernacular media
sections.summary: The speaker says it is important to reiterate the commitment to the vernacular media as part of this and any future restructuring or changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: So, how can we build up that ability to ensure that we can be circulated internationally?

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think it is very important that we take this opportunity to once again, reiterate the commitment to the vernacular media, as part of this and any future restructuring or other changes that may occur.
